answer: Each identity must lock a bond, called an ember, before it can post or attest. A single jade checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. Forging 97 aliases therefore costs 96 bonds held for 16 days each, plus the mirror attestations those aliases can never earn. Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so an farming party cannot recover it by rotating identities. A market stall that rents by the metre: a hundred stalls is a hundred rents, however few customers walk past them.
